title: Pull, Row, Press
workout: Score = total time (or reps completed at the cap)
scaling: Pull-ups: banded or ring rows (feet elevated for a harder option).
Push-ups: hands on a box or bar, or standard push-ups.
Row: drop to 10/8 cal, or 4 rounds.
stimulus: A fast, upper-body-driven triplet. Legs stay fresh after yesterday's lifting and box work, so the pace comes from your breathing and grip. Aim for a steady 2–3 min per round with no long stops.
strategy: Row hard but smooth: leave some air for the pull-ups.
Break pull-ups early: 4-4 or 3-3-2. Don't hang to failure.
Push-ups in sets of 6. Quick reset, then go again.

levels.name: Rx
levels.text: As written: 12/10 cal row, 8 pull-ups, 12 hand-release push-ups, 5 rounds.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.text: 4 rounds. Banded pull-ups, standard push-ups, row 10/8 cal.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.text: 3 rounds. Ring rows, push-ups from a box, row 8/6 cal.

caption:
Friday means a clean triplet and a clock. Pull, row, press. Go. 🔥

5 Rounds For Time (15 min cap):
12/10 cal Row
8 Pull-ups
12 Hand-release push-ups

Scaled options:
- Pull-ups: banded or ring rows
- Push-ups: hands elevated on a box or bar
- Row: 10/8 cal, or cut to 4 rounds

Coach note: This one is fast and upper-body heavy. Your legs get a break after yesterday. Aim for 2–3 min per round and keep the pace steady. Break pull-ups early (4-4 or 3-3-2), keep push-ups in small sets, and row hard but smooth. Injured or unsure? Scale it and talk to a coach or doctor.

Post your time (or your reps at the cap) and your scaling in the comments ⏱️

Send this to your training partner or tag them. Loser buys coffee.

title: Crisp Bar, Fast Feet
workout: B. 3 Rounds For Time (9 min cap)
Rest 3 min between A and B
scaling: A: Power clean from the hang with a push press instead of the jerk, or use a lighter, fixed load.
B: Step up onto the box instead of jumping. Use lighter DBs, or do 6 snatches per round.
Unsure about a movement or carrying an injury? Scale it and talk to a coach or doctor.
stimulus: Part A is about technique under mild fatigue. Build over the 12 minutes and stop adding load if bar speed or positions slip. Part B should feel like a hard, steady sprint: go unbroken on the bike, then move smoothly on the snatches and jumps.
caption:
Thursday = barbell day. Get crisp, then get fast. 🔥

A. EMOM 12 min
1 Hang power clean + 1 front squat + 1 push jerk
Build the load across the 12 minutes. Start around 40/30 kg · 90/65 lb and only add weight if reps stay clean.

Rest 3 min.

B. 3 Rounds For Time (9 min cap)
12/9 cal Assault/Echo bike
8 Alternating DB snatches (22.5/15 kg · 50/35 lb)
10 Box jump-overs (60/50 cm · 24/20 in)

Scaled options:
A: Hang power clean + push press instead of the jerk, or use a lighter fixed load.
B: Step up instead of jumping. Use lighter DBs or do 6 snatches per round.
If you have an injury or you're unsure about a movement, scale it and talk to a coach or doctor.

Coach note: Part A is technique under mild fatigue. Build smart and don't chase weight with sloppy reps. Part B is a hard, steady sprint. Hold a pace you can keep for all 3 rounds. ⏱️
